care: Sow at 2–5 cm depth with even spacing
Irrigate at crown-root and flowering stages
Watch for rust and aphids; rotate crops yearly
crops.desc: Wheat is the world's most widely grown cereal and the backbone of breads, rotis and noodles across continents. Its slender stalks turn from green to gold as the grain ripens, signalling harvest time.
facts: Wheat was first farmed about 10,000 years ago in the Fertile Crescent.
One wheat plant can produce 30–50 grains per head.
grows: Cool-season crop; sown in winter in South Asia
Needs 50–75 cm of rainfall or irrigation
crops.name: Wheat
crops.tagline: The golden grain behind every roti.
crops.tagline_hi: हर रोटी के पीछे का सुनहरा अनाज।
uses: Flour for roti, bread, noodles and pasta
Straw used as animal bedding and mulch
Bran as fibre-rich animal and human food

care: Keep 2–5 cm standing water till grain-fill
Drain before harvest; guard against stem borer
crops.desc: Rice feeds more people than any other crop. Grown in flooded paddies, its young green shoots reflect the sky until the fields turn amber with ripening grain.
facts: There are over 40,000 cultivated varieties of rice.
Rice paddies are nurseries for fish and ducks in many regions.
grows: Clayey soil that holds standing water
crops.name: Rice
crops.tagline: The flooded-field grain feeding half the planet.
crops.tagline_hi: आधे ग्रह का पेट भरने वाला धान।
uses: Steamed rice, biryani, idli and dosa batter
Husk as fuel and straw as fodder

care: Sow after frost risk passes, 60 cm rows
Needs nitrogen — side-dress at knee height
crops.desc: Maize, or corn, towers over most cereals with its broad leaves and golden cobs wrapped in husk. It is eaten fresh, ground into flour, and widely used as animal feed and industrial starch.
facts: Each silk strand connects to one kernel — unpollinated silks mean missing kernels.
Maize is the highest-yielding cereal per hectare on average.
crops.name: Maize
crops.tagline: The tall American grain that became global.
crops.tagline_hi: वह लंबा अमेरिकी अनाज जो वैश्विक बन गया।
uses: Roasted bhutta, makki roti and popcorn

care: Sow with the first monsoon showers
crops.desc: Pearl millet, or bajra, thrives where other cereals fail — in hot, sandy soils with little rain. Its candle-like seed heads are a familiar sight across Rajasthan, Gujarat and the Sahel.
facts: Bajra has more iron and fibre than polished rice.
It matures in just 70–90 days, escaping late-season drought.
crops.name: Pearl Millet
crops.tagline: The desert grain that laughs at drought.
crops.tagline_hi: सूखे को मात देने वाला रेगिस्तानी अनाज।

care: Weed early; ragi competes poorly at first
Harvest when heads turn brown and dry
crops.desc: Finger millet, or ragi, grows finger-like clusters of small reddish grains. A staple in Karnataka and parts of Africa, it is prized for calcium and slow-release energy.
facts: Ragi has about three times the calcium of wheat.
Its grains store for years without spoiling — a traditional famine reserve.
crops.name: Finger Millet
crops.tagline: Tiny reddish grains, mighty nutrition.
crops.tagline_hi: छोटे लाल दाने, बड़ा पोषण।

care: Thin to one strong plant per spot
Birds love ripening heads — net if needed
crops.desc: Sorghum, or jowar, stands tall with waxy leaves that shrug off heat. A staple across Maharashtra and sub-Saharan Africa, its grain becomes bhakri and porridge.
facts: Sorghum leaves roll up in drought to save water, then unroll after rain.
It is the world's fifth most produced cereal.
crops.name: Sorghum
crops.tagline: The camel of cereals — built for heat.
crops.tagline_hi: अनाजों का ऊँट — गर्मी के लिए बना।

care: Avoid excess irrigation — it invites wilt
Rotate with cereals to break pest cycles
crops.desc: Chickpea is India's most loved pulse — the base of chana masala, hummus and roasted snacks. Its small bushy plants fix nitrogen, leaving the soil richer than they found it.
facts: India grows about 70% of the world's chickpeas.
Chickpea leaves taste tangy — they contain malic acid.
crops.name: Chickpea
crops.tagline: The humble gram behind chana masala.
crops.tagline_hi: छोले मसाले के पीछे का विनम्र चना।
uses: Besan (gram flour) for pakoras and sweets

care: One or two light irrigations suffice
crops.desc: Lentils cook faster than any other pulse, melting into creamy dals. Their delicate plants carry small pods with flat, lens-shaped seeds in shades of red, green and brown.
facts: Red lentils cook in 15–20 minutes without soaking.
Lentils are among the oldest cultivated foods — over 9,000 years.
crops.name: Lentil
crops.tagline: Tiny lens-shaped seeds, giant comfort in dal.
crops.tagline_hi: छोटे दाल के दाने, दाल में बड़ा सुकून।

care: Sow at monsoon onset, wide spacing
Nip the top to encourage branching
Pick pods as they mature for longer harvest
crops.desc: Pigeon pea, or toor/arhar, grows into a woody shrub taller than a person, dotted with yellow-red flowers. Its dal is the everyday protein of millions of thalis.
facts: A single pigeon pea plant can live and yield for 3–5 years.
It is often intercropped with millets and oilseeds.
crops.name: Pigeon Pea
crops.tagline: The tall dal plant of the monsoon fields.
crops.tagline_hi: मानसूनी खेतों का लंबा दाल वाला पौधा।
uses: Toor dal — the classic yellow dal
Stems as firewood, leaves as fodder

care: Sow by October for best yields
Harvest when pods turn yellow, before shattering
crops.desc: In winter, mustard paints entire districts yellow. Its tiny seeds are crushed into the pungent oil of North Indian kitchens, while the leaves become sarson da saag.
facts: Mustard oil's pungency comes from allyl isothiocyanate.
The flowers are a major winter forage for honeybees.
crops.name: Mustard
crops.tagline: Yellow seas of winter flowers, pungent oil.
crops.tagline_hi: सर्दियों के पीले फूलों का समंदर, तीखा तेल।
uses: Mustard oil for cooking and massage
Sarson da saag from the leaves

care: Ensure loose soil for pods to enter
Harvest when leaves yellow; dry pods well
crops.desc: Groundnut flowers above ground, then does something extraordinary — its stalks bend down and push the young pods into the soil to ripen. Digging them up at harvest is half the fun.
facts: Groundnut is a legume, not a true nut — cousin of the pea.
The burying stalks are called pegs, or gynophores.
grows: Light sandy loam for easy pegging
crops.name: Groundnut
crops.tagline: The nut that ripens underground.
crops.tagline_hi: वह मूँगफली जो ज़मीन के नीचे पकती है।
uses: Cake left after oil as protein feed

care: Support tall stems in windy spots
Harvest when heads droop and backs yellow
crops.desc: Young sunflowers famously turn their heads to follow the sun across the sky. Their giant golden discs ripen into striped seeds rich in light, heart-friendly oil.
facts: A sunflower head can hold up to 2,000 seeds.
Only young buds track the sun; mature heads face east.
crops.name: Sunflower
crops.tagline: The flower that tracks the sun.
crops.tagline_hi: वह फूल जो सूरज का पीछा करता है।

care: Stake or cage to keep fruit off soil
Water at the base; avoid wetting leaves
Pinch side shoots for bigger tomatoes
crops.desc: Tomato plants sprawl with fragrant, slightly sticky leaves and clusters of fruit that ripen from green to sunset red. Botanically a berry, it is cooked as the world's favourite vegetable.
facts: There are over 10,000 tomato varieties, from cherry to beefsteak.
Tomatoes ripen faster next to bananas — the ethylene gas helps.
crops.name: Tomato
crops.tagline: The berry the world cooks as a vegetable.
crops.tagline_hi: वह बेरी जिसे दुनिया सब्ज़ी बनाकर खाती है।

care: Hill soil around stems as they grow
Cure tubers in shade before storing
crops.desc: Potato grows its treasure underground — swollen stem tips we call tubers. Above, it looks unremarkable; below, a single plant can hide a dozen potatoes.
facts: Potatoes were first farmed in the Andes 7,000+ years ago.
Green potatoes contain solanine — store them in the dark.
grows: Loose, well-drained soil for tuber growth
crops.name: Potato
crops.tagline: Buried treasure from the Andes.
crops.tagline_hi: एंडीज़ से आया दबा हुआ खज़ाना।

care: Keep beds weed-free; onions hate competition
Harvest when tops fall over naturally
crops.desc: Onion begins as a slender green shoot and swells into layered bulbs underground. Slice one and your eyes water — that's the plant's chemical defence, and the start of every good tadka.
facts: Onions were worshipped in ancient Egypt as symbols of eternity.
The tear gas is a compound called syn-propanethial-S-oxide.
crops.name: Onion
crops.tagline: Layers of flavour, tears of joy.
crops.tagline_hi: स्वाद की परतें, खुशी के आँसू।
uses: Base of curries via onion-tomato masala

care: Plant grafted saplings for true-to-type fruit
Water young trees; mature ones are hardy
crops.desc: The mango tree can live a century, spreading a broad canopy over village courtyards. Its fruit — fragrant, golden, unapologetically juicy — is called the king of fruits for good reason.
facts: A mango tree can produce fruit for 40+ years.
India grows over 1,000 mango varieties, from Alphonso to Dasheri.
grows: Dry spell before flowering helps fruit set
crops.name: Mango
crops.tagline: The king of fruits, crowned every summer.
crops.tagline_hi: फलों का राजा, हर गर्मी में ताजपोशी।
uses: Wood and shade from the tree

crops.desc: The banana 'tree' is actually the world's largest herb — its trunk is tightly wrapped leaf bases. Bunches emerge from the heart of the crown, curving upward toward the sun.
facts: Bananas are berries; strawberries, botanically, are not.
Wild bananas are full of hard seeds; cultivated ones are seedless.
crops.name: Banana
crops.tagline: The giant herb's curved gift.
crops.tagline_hi: विशाल शाक का मुड़ा हुआ उपहार।

care: Prune to keep a manageable canopy
Bag fruits to protect from fruit fly
crops.desc: Guava is the unfussy orchard tree — it fruits young, fruits often, and shrugs off neglect. Cut one open to find pink or white flesh studded with tiny hard seeds around a sweet heart.
facts: One guava can hold four times the vitamin C of an orange.
Guava leaves are brewed as a traditional digestive tea.
crops.name: Guava
crops.tagline: The hardy orchard fruit with a fragrant heart.
crops.tagline_hi: सुगंधित दिल वाला मज़बूत बाग़ी फल।

care: Plant rhizome pieces in warm soil
crops.desc: Turmeric hides its gold underground. The plant's broad leaves look like a small banana grove; below, orange rhizomes wait to be boiled, dried and ground into the spice that colours half the world's curries.
facts: Turmeric's colour comes from curcumin, studied for anti-inflammatory properties.
It takes about 5 kg of fresh rhizome to make 1 kg of powder.
crops.name: Turmeric
crops.tagline: Underground gold that colours the curry.
crops.tagline_hi: ज़मीन के नीचे का सोना जो करी को रंग देता है।
uses: Natural dye for cloth and food

crops.desc: Cumin grows as a delicate, feathery annual barely knee-high, yet its tiny ridged seeds carry the warm, earthy aroma of tadkas, garam masala and street chaat.
facts: Cumin seeds are actually dried fruits, each holding one seed.
It was found in 4,000-year-old Egyptian tombs.
crops.name: Cumin
crops.tagline: Tiny seeds, the soul of the tadka.
crops.tagline_hi: छोटे दाने, तड़के की जान।

care: Pick capsules as they ripen, in rounds
crops.desc: Cardamom, the queen of spices, grows in misty mountain shade on tall reed-like stems. Its green pods hide intensely fragrant black seeds — a little perfumes a whole pot of chai.
facts: Cardamom is the world's third most expensive spice, after saffron and vanilla.
Wild elephants disperse its seeds in Western Ghats forests.
crops.name: Cardamom
crops.tagline: The queen of spices from misty hills.
crops.tagline_hi: धुंधली पहाड़ियों से मसालों की रानी।

care: One deep watering beats many shallow ones
Pick bolls as they open to keep lint clean
crops.desc: Cotton's magic is in the boll — a pod that bursts into soft white fluff, each fibre a single elongated seed hair. That cloud becomes the thread of t-shirts and saris.
facts: One cotton boll holds about 250,000 fibres.
Cotton fibre is 95% cellulose — almost pure.
crops.name: Cotton
crops.tagline: Clouds in a boll, thread for the world.
crops.tagline_hi: डोडे में बादल, दुनिया के लिए धागा।

care: Earth up as shoots grow tall
crops.desc: Sugarcane is a giant grass whose jointed stalks store pure sweetness. Chew a stalk and you taste sunshine converted to sugar — the same sweetness that fills mills at harvest season.
facts: Sugarcane can grow 5 metres tall in a single season.
Bagasse, the crushed stalk, fuels the sugar mill itself.
grows: Rich loam with plenty of water
crops.name: Sugarcane
crops.tagline: Sweet stalks of a giant grass.
crops.tagline_hi: विशाल घास के मीठे तने।

care: Pluck the top two leaves and a bud
Shade young plants in hot zones
crops.desc: Tea is an evergreen shrub kept pruned to a neat picking table on misty hillsides. Every cup — green, black or oolong — begins as the same tender top leaves, transformed by withering and rolling.
facts: Tea is the world's most drunk beverage after water.
The same leaf makes green, black and oolong tea — processing differs.
crops.name: Tea
crops.tagline: Misty hillsides in a cup.
crops.tagline_hi: प्याले में धुंधली पहाड़ियाँ।

care: Cut at early bloom for best protein
crops.desc: Alfalfa, or rizka, is the queen of fodders — a deep-rooted legume cut again and again through the season. Its purple flower spikes feed bees while its leaves pack protein for dairy animals.
facts: Alfalfa roots can reach 4–5 metres deep.
It fixes nitrogen, enriching soil for the next crop.
crops.name: Alfalfa
crops.tagline: The protein-rich queen of fodders.
crops.tagline_hi: चारे की प्रोटीन-भरी रानी।
uses: Green fodder and hay for dairy cattle

care: Plant stem cuttings at monsoon onset
Cut every 45–60 days at 1 m height
crops.desc: Napier grass is a fodder giant — thick clumps of tall stems that can be cut five or six times a year. Chop-and-carry farmers rely on it to keep buffaloes milking through every season.
facts: Hybrid napier can yield 200+ tonnes of green fodder per hectare yearly.
It is also planted as a trap crop for stem borers in maize.
crops.name: Napier Grass
crops.tagline: The cut-and-come-again fodder giant.
crops.tagline_hi: काटो और फिर उगाओ — चारे का दानव।

care: Pick pods young for vegetable use
crops.desc: Cowpea, or lobia, is the multitasker of the monsoon field — its young pods are a vegetable, its dry seeds a pulse, and its leafy vines excellent fodder. Goats follow it like fans.
facts: Cowpea tolerates heat and drought better than most legumes.
It matures grain in as little as 60 days.
crops.name: Cowpea
crops.tagline: One plant: vegetable, pulse and fodder.
crops.tagline_hi: एक पौधा: सब्ज़ी, दाल और चारा।

care: Water deeply, then let dry fully
Repot pups into their own pots
crops.desc: Aloe vera stores water in its thick, serrated leaves — a desert survival trick that also gives us the cooling gel inside. Snap a leaf and the clear gel is ready for skin and hair.
facts: Aloe gel is 99% water, plus vitamins and enzymes.
It closes its leaf pores at night to save water — a CAM plant.
crops.name: Aloe Vera
crops.tagline: Desert leaves hiding cooling gel.
crops.tagline_hi: रेगिस्तानी पत्तों में छिपा ठंडक वाला जेल।

care: Sow in warm soil after spring
Pinch flowers to keep leaves coming
Protect from frost; mulch in winter
crops.desc: Tulsi grows in courtyards and temples across India, its clove-scented leaves brewed into kadha at the first sign of a cold. Bees adore its tiny purple-white flower spikes.
facts: Tulsi is an adaptogen, traditionally used against stress.
Its scent comes from eugenol — also found in cloves.
crops.name: Tulsi
crops.tagline: The sacred basil of courtyards and kadha.
crops.tagline_hi: आँगन और काढ़े की पवित्र तुलसी।
uses: Sacred plant in homes and temples

care: Sow in nursery, transplant at rains
crops.desc: Ashwagandha is a modest shrub with dull green leaves and orange-red berries — but its roots are the star, dried and powdered as one of Ayurveda's most famous rejuvenating herbs.
facts: Its name means 'smell of a horse' — said to impart stallion strength.
It is now studied worldwide for stress and sleep.
crops.name: Ashwagandha
crops.tagline: Humble shrub, legendary root.
crops.tagline_hi: विनम्र झाड़ी, प्रसिद्ध जड़।

crops.desc: Marigold's pom-pom blooms in marigold-orange and yellow are the flowers of Indian celebration — strung into torans, offered at temples, and brightening winter gardens everywhere.
facts: Marigold roots repel nematodes — farmers plant them as guards.
Its petals are edible and used as natural food colour.
crops.name: Marigold
crops.tagline: The festival flower of torans and temples.
crops.tagline_hi: तोरण और मंदिरों का त्योहारी फूल।

care: Watch for aphids and black spot
crops.desc: The rose needs little introduction — layered petals, thorned stems, and a perfume that launched industries. Damask roses fill Kannauj's fields for attar; garden roses fill vases.
facts: Rose hips have more vitamin C than citrus.
Attar of roses takes 4 tonnes of petals per litre of oil.
crops.name: Rose
crops.tagline: Thorns guarding the queen of flowers.
crops.tagline_hi: फूलों की रानी की रखवाली करते काँटे।

crops.desc: Hibiscus trumpets open for a single glorious day — huge, papery blooms in reds and pinks, each with a dramatic central column of stamens. Then it simply makes another.
facts: Hibiscus flowers are edible — used in teas and salads.
In many places each bloom lasts just one day.
crops.name: Hibiscus
crops.tagline: One-day trumpets, endless encore.
crops.tagline_hi: एक दिन के तुरही फूल, अनंत प्रस्तुति।

care: Trim long vines to bush out
crops.desc: The money plant is the survivor of indoor gardening — heart-shaped leaves trailing from a bottle of water on countless office desks. It roots from almost any cutting.
facts: NASA listed it among top air-purifying plants.
It can grow in just water for months.
crops.name: Money Plant
crops.tagline: The unkillable desk companion.
crops.tagline_hi: न मरने वाला डेस्क साथी।

care: Repot only when bursting the pot
crops.desc: The snake plant stands like a cluster of swords — stiff, upright, patterned leaves that thrive on neglect. It is the plant you buy for someone who kills plants.
facts: It converts CO2 at night, unlike most plants.
It can survive weeks without water.
crops.name: Snake Plant
crops.tagline: Swords that thrive on neglect.
crops.tagline_hi: लापरवाही में पनपने वाली तलवारें।
uses: Fibre from leaves in some regions

crops.desc: The areca palm brings the tropics indoors — feathery fronds arching from clustered golden stems. Offices and malls love it; so do cats, since it is non-toxic to pets.
facts: It is one of the most popular indoor palms worldwide.
In the wild it can reach 10 metres tall.
crops.name: Areca Palm
crops.tagline: A pocket of tropics for your living room.
crops.tagline_hi: आपके लिविंग रूम के लिए उष्णकटिबंध की झलक।

crops.desc: Neem is the village pharmacy — bitter leaves, oil-rich seeds, and bark used in remedies for centuries. Its light shade cools courtyards while its flowers feed bees.
facts: Neem oil's azadirachtin disrupts insect growth — a natural pesticide.
A mature neem can live 200 years.
crops.name: Neem
crops.tagline: The village pharmacy in tree form.
crops.tagline_hi: पेड़ के रूप में गाँव की फार्मेसी।

care: Aerial roots need room to descend
crops.desc: The banyan begins as a seed in a crack and becomes a forest unto itself — aerial roots descending to form new trunks until one tree covers an acre. Village councils met under banyans for centuries.
facts: Some banyans cover over 4 acres — among the world's widest canopies.
It is India's national tree.
crops.name: Banyan
crops.tagline: One tree that becomes a forest.
crops.tagline_hi: एक पेड़ जो जंगल बन जाता है।

crops.desc: The peepal's heart-shaped leaves tremble in the slightest breeze, making a soft rustling music. Sacred to Buddhists, Hindus and Jains, ancient peepals anchor countless village shrines.
facts: The Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal (bodhi tree).
Its leaves flutter due to long, flexible stalks.
crops.name: Peepal
crops.tagline: The trembling leaves of the bodhi tree.
crops.tagline_hi: बोधि वृक्ष के काँपते पत्ते।

site.name: Fasal
site.tagline: Field notes on the crops behind everyday life.
site.tagline_hi: रोज़मर्रा के जीवन के पीछे की फ़सलों पर फ़ील्ड नोट्स।
